This behavior was mainly due to the fact that some receptor conformations could lodge certain ligands remarkably well but could dump those which required a different binding site rearrangement. For example, type I protein kinase inhibitor 1 (5,7 diphenylpyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine, Figure 1B) ranked 6th when screened using a conformation of the proto-oncogene tyrosine protein kinase SRC (SRC_HUMAN) co-crystallized in complex with a ligand very similar to 1 (PDBid: 1YOL, see also Figure S1A in the Supporting Information). p1_b5.ocr: first example clearly shows the fundamental role of taking into account several receptor conformations for relatively flexible protein families (such as kinases). In a further case study, a selective modulator (2) of the progesterone receptor (PRG_HUMAN) was ranked 2nd when docked using the conformation solved in complex with Asoprisnil (PDBid: 2OVH). The exceptionally high score could be achieved since the N,N-dimethylanilino substituent of 2 could almost perfectly fill an accessory pocket created by the conformational rearrangement of Met909 side chain. Remarkably, in this case too, 2 and the ligand co-crystallized in 2OVH were structurally very similar (see also Figure S1B in the Supporting Information).
